(ticker GILD), and list its competitors. Use the most recent information you know. Never invent figures: use null when unsure. Be specific (products, numbers, years).

   (approximate latest fiscal-year figures for the company itself and for every listed competitor; decimals, e.g. 0.42; null if unknown),

                   "rows": [ {"name": "company name", "latest": decimal or null, "earlier": decimal or null} ] } ]  (up to 3 of its main markets, the company and its main rivals),
 "threats": ["specific things that could weaken its advantage"],
 "ceo": {"name": "current CEO", "founder": true or false, "since": "YYYY", "background": "e.g. electrical engineer, Stanford MBA"},
 "checklist": { "<id>": {"verdict": "yes|partly|no|unknown", "evidence": "one specific sentence with names, numbers or examples"} }  for EVERY id below:
   "c1": Rule Breaker #1: is it the leader of an important industry that is still emerging and growing fast?
   "c2": Rule Breaker #2: why do customers choose it over rivals (brand, better value, innovation, culture, leadership), and is that advantage hard to copy and likely to last many years?

Start the evidence with those words in quotes (e.g. “innovative, premium, reliable”), then say whether that impression is mostly positive.

}

result.name: Gilead Sciences, Inc.
result.industry: Biopharmaceuticals (HIV, liver disease, oncology and cell therapy)
markets: Viral hepatitis (HBV, HCV, HDV) and primary biliary cholangitis
CAR-T cell therapy for blood cancers

mission.statement: To discover, develop and deliver innovative therapeutics for people with life-threatening diseases
mission.source: Gilead company website (gilead.com/company), alongside its vision "To create a healthier world for all people"
mission.plain: Gilead wants to invent and bring to patients new medicines for the most deadly diseases.

about.plain: Gilead is a big medicine company from California. Its best-known pills let people with HIV live long, healthy lives with one pill a day. It also makes medicines that stop people from catching HIV, including a shot given only twice a year. It also sells medicines for liver infections and some cancers, including treatments that reprogram a patient's own immune cells to fight cancer.
about.customers: Drug wholesalers, pharmacies, hospitals and cancer centers buy its medicines, which are mostly paid for by insurers and governments for patients.
about.everyday: Biktarvy, the one-a-day HIV pill often advertised on US television, is Gilead's biggest product, and remdesivir (Veklury) was one of the first COVID-19 treatments used in hospitals.

money.plain: Biktarvy daily pill ($14.3B in 2025), Descovy for treatment and prevention, and other HIV pills
Hepatitis B and C pills, Hepcludex for hepatitis delta, Livdelzi for a rare liver disease
Yescarta and Tecartus, made from a patient's own immune cells
Trodelvy, a targeted drug for hard-to-treat breast cancer
Yeztugo (lenacapavir), launched in 2025; sales of $232M in Q2 2026
anito-cel, a CAR-T for multiple myeloma gained by buying Arcellx for about $7.8B in April 2026; not yet approved

result.summary: Gilead has a strong, durable moat in HIV: Biktarvy alone sold $14.3B in 2025, Gilead's HIV franchise grew to $20.8B, and patent settlements mean no US generic Biktarvy is expected before April 1, 2036. Long-acting lenacapavir (Yeztugo) extends that lead into prevention, while its oncology and cell-therapy businesses are smaller and face heavier competition. Its weakness is concentration: about 70% of 2025 revenue came from HIV.

pricingPower.evidence: Gilead attributed Q2 2026 HIV sales growth of 12% (to $5,693M) primarily to higher average realized price and demand, and Descovy's 48% jump (to $967M) also to higher realized price and demand, so price rises came with rising volumes; offsets include IRA Medicare Part D reform, a most-favored-nation pricing agreement with the US government and payer-mix shifts it lists as risks.

moats.evidence: Patents and settlements protect Biktarvy from US generics until at least April 1, 2036, and Gilead's HIV brands (Biktarvy, Descovy, Yeztugo) are the reference products for doctors; HIV product sales reached $20,752M in 2025.

Patients whose HIV is fully suppressed on a well-tolerated single pill like Biktarvy are rarely switched by their doctors, because switching risks side effects or loss of viral control, which keeps revenue sticky for decades.
Medicines do not become more valuable to one patient because more patients use them.

With $29.4B of 2025 revenue and a 78.8% gross margin, Gilead can fund $5.8B of yearly R&D and a large HIV salesforce, but small-molecule pills are not inherently cheaper for it to make than for rivals.
The HIV market is effectively a two-player field (Gilead and GSK's ViiV Healthcare), which limits price competition among branded regimens.
Long-acting twice-yearly lenacapavir prevention is a new format, but incumbents such as ViiV (Apretude) can and do pursue long-acting products too.

Decades of antiviral chemistry produced tenofovir, sofosbuvir, bictegravir and lenacapavir, and Kite's cell-therapy manufacturing network delivers personalised CAR-T at scale, both hard to replicate quickly.
Lenacapavir, the first capsid inhibitor, is exclusive to Gilead and underpins both Yeztugo and its next-generation long-acting HIV pipeline.

customers.evidence: Biktarvy sales rose from $13,423M in 2024 to $14,334M in 2025 and to $3,772M in Q2 2026 (+7%), showing patients stay on therapy; a Trefis analysis reported more than 70% of early Yeztugo users returned for their second six-monthly dose.

talent.evidence: Gilead has been named one of Newsweek's America's Greatest Workplaces for Diversity and one of JUST Capital/CNBC's America's Most JUST Companies, and Gilead Spain was certified a Top Employer, but it is not a fixture at the top of broad employer rankings.

product.evidence: Biktarvy is the largest-selling HIV medicine and Yeztugo is the first twice-yearly injection for HIV prevention approved by the FDA; in oncology, Trodelvy won FDA approval for first-line metastatic triple-negative breast cancer in 2026, while Yescarta and Tecartus are losing ground to in- and out-of-class competition.

competitors.name: ViiV Healthcare (majority-owned by GSK)
competitors.note: The other major HIV company: Dovato, Triumeq and long-acting Cabenuva in treatment and Apretude injectable PrEP against Biktarvy, Descovy and Yeztugo.

competitors.name: Merck & Co.
competitors.note: HIV (doravirine, islatravir regimens, though partnered with Gilead on islatravir/lenacapavir); Keytruda in breast cancer alongside and against Trodelvy.

competitors.name: Johnson & Johnson
competitors.note: Carvykti CAR-T (with Legend Biotech) is the incumbent in multiple myeloma that anito-cel must beat; rilpivirine-based HIV drugs.

competitors.name: Bristol Myers Squibb
competitors.note: Breyanzi and Abecma CAR-T therapies compete with Yescarta, Tecartus and anito-cel in lymphoma and myeloma.

competitors.name: AstraZeneca
competitors.note: Enhertu and Datroway (with Daiichi Sankyo) compete with Trodelvy in breast cancer; Imfinzi in other tumours.

competitors.name: Daiichi Sankyo
competitors.note: Co-developer of Enhertu and Datroway antibody-drug conjugates competing with Trodelvy; does not file with the SEC.

competitors.name: Legend Biotech
competitors.note: Partner of J&J on Carvykti, the BCMA CAR-T rival to anito-cel.

competitors.name: Novartis
competitors.note: Kymriah CAR-T in lymphoma and breast-cancer drugs.

competitors.name: AbbVie
competitors.note: Mavyret competes with Gilead's Epclusa and Harvoni in hepatitis C; Epkinly (with Genmab) bispecific competes with CAR-T in lymphoma.

competitors.name: Ipsen
competitors.note: Iqirvo competes with Livdelzi in primary biliary cholangitis; does not file with the SEC.

competitors.name: Pfizer
competitors.note: Paxlovid competes with Veklury in COVID-19; minority owner of ViiV Healthcare.

competitors.name: Teva Pharmaceutical
competitors.note: Generic HIV and hepatitis medicines compete with Gilead's older off-patent products.

threats: Concentration: HIV was 70% of 2025 revenue and Biktarvy alone 49%, so any HIV setback hits the whole company.

US drug-pricing policy: IRA Medicare Part D reform and price negotiation, the most-favored-nation pricing agreement with the US government, expiring ACA subsidies and shifts to more discounted payers.
Long-acting HIV competition from ViiV Healthcare (Cabenuva, Apretude and next-generation regimens) and Merck.
Cell therapy erosion: Yescarta and Tecartus sales fell in 2025 and Q2 2026 because of in- and out-of-class competition, including bispecific antibodies.
Execution risk on roughly $12.6B of 2026 acquisitions (Arcellx about $7.8B, Tubulis $3.15B upfront, Ouro $1.675B upfront), which pushed Gilead to a guided 2026 GAAP loss and raised debt to $26.2B.
Pipeline setbacks such as the stopped Phase 3 EVOKE-03 trial of Trodelvy plus Keytruda in first-line lung cancer.
Eventual generic entry for Biktarvy (not before April 1, 2036 in the US) and Descovy.

ceo.name: Daniel O'Day
ceo.background: Biology degree from Georgetown and Columbia MBA; more than 30 years at Roche, ending as CEO of Roche Pharmaceuticals

c1.evidence: Gilead leads the HIV market (HIV product sales $20,752M in 2025), an important but mature industry, though long-acting PrEP with Yeztugo is a newer, fast-growing segment.

c2.evidence: Doctors choose Biktarvy for its single once-daily pill with strong efficacy and a high barrier to resistance, and that lead is protected by patent settlements delaying US generics until April 1, 2036 plus Gilead's lenacapavir long-acting pipeline.

c3.evidence: Gilead is the default leader in HIV medicine and well known among patients and doctors, but most ordinary consumers do not know the company name the way they know Google or Netflix.

c4.evidence: Its mission, "To discover, develop and deliver innovative therapeutics for people with life-threatening diseases," and its stated goal of helping end the HIV epidemic are emphasised often, but Gilead is also a profit-driven big pharma that has faced criticism over HIV and hepatitis C drug prices.

c6.evidence: “HIV pills, expensive drugs, remdesivir” are the words many people associate with Gilead; the impression is mixed, with respect for its HIV and hepatitis C cures offset by criticism of high US drug prices.

c7.evidence: HIV treatment and prevention keep growing (Gilead's HIV sales rose 12% in Q2 2026 to $5,693M and its PrEP sales passed $1B in a quarter), but this is not a fast-expanding secular trend on the scale of AI or cloud.

c8.evidence: Gilead is expanding into oncology and cell therapy through acquisitions (Arcellx's anito-cel for myeloma, Tubulis antibody-drug conjugates, Ouro) and into once-weekly oral HIV prevention (FDA decision due February 2, 2027).

m1.evidence: Daniel O'Day has set out a clear goal of transforming HIV prevention with long-acting lenacapavir and building an oncology franchise, but he is a seasoned operator rather than a visionary founder.

m2.evidence: O'Day is a professional manager who joined in March 2019 after more than 30 years at Roche; he is not a founder, although he has steered long-term R&D bets such as lenacapavir.

m4.evidence: There is no specific, verifiable evidence that O'Day leads in a distinctively servant-leader style beyond standard corporate statements.

m5.evidence: Under O'Day Gilead produced lenacapavir, the first capsid inhibitor, but much of its newer innovation has been bought (Immunomedics, Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro) rather than invented in-house.

m6.evidence: O'Day has a biology degree and decades in pharma and diagnostics, but he is a commercial executive (Columbia MBA) rather than a scientist or engineer.

m7.evidence: Gilead under O'Day has licensed lenacapavir to generic makers for low-income countries and donated remdesivir supplies early in the pandemic, alongside the usual profit focus of a large drug company.

m7b.evidence: No record was found of O'Day giving a commencement speech at a top university.

m8b.evidence: O'Day keeps a conventional, low-profile big-pharma CEO style rather than a distinctive public persona.

m9.evidence: Since O'Day took over in 2019, revenue rose from $24,689M (2020) to $29,443M (2025), Biktarvy grew to $14,334M, Yeztugo was approved and launched, and the stock rose about 32% over the last 52 weeks to $156.19.

m10.evidence: Gilead is not known for frugality; it spent $5,774M on SG&A in 2025 and pays large sums for acquisitions such as the roughly $7.8B Arcellx deal.

c10.evidence: Gilead's HIV medicines turned HIV into a manageable condition for millions of people worldwide, its sofosbuvir drugs cure hepatitis C, and generic licences extend lenacapavir prevention to low-income countries.

p2.evidence: Discovering drugs like lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention shot, and manufacturing personalised CAR-T therapies are extremely hard scientific feats that matter for public health.

f2.evidence: Gross margin fell from 81.5% in 2020 to 78.8% in 2025, and operating margin swung widely (36.3% in 2021, 5.8% in 2024 after IPR&D charges, 34.0% in 2025) rather than rising steadily.

f3.evidence: At June 30, 2026 debt was $26,246M against $3,179M of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, though 2025 free cash flow of $9,456M services it comfortably and stockholders' equity was positive at $11,744M.

f4.evidence: Operating income rose from $4,071M in 2020 to $10,022M in 2025 and operating cash flow from $8,168M to $10,019M, but both were volatile in between (operating cash flow peaked at $11,384M in 2021).

v1.evidence: In HIV, Biktarvy offers a complete regimen in one small daily pill with few drug interactions and strong resistance protection, the practical reason it is the best-selling HIV medicine.

v2.evidence: Gilead has been named among Newsweek's America's Greatest Workplaces for Diversity and JUST Capital's America's Most JUST Companies, but no evidence was found of it ranking near the top of broad employer lists such as Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For.

c5.evidence: If Gilead disappeared, millions of people living with HIV who rely on Biktarvy, Descovy and other Gilead regimens, and people using its PrEP to stay HIV-negative, would lose their medicines of choice.
